title: Interpreter initialization from a serialized header
statement: Let $x$ be a bit string, let $p$ be an input-head position on $x$, and let $\beta$, $\rho$, and $T$ be bit strings with $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $T=\langle\beta,1^n\,0\,\rho\rangle$, where $1^n$ denotes a string of $n$ ones. After exactly $|T|+2|\beta|+2n+7$ steps from the interpreter's entry configuration with table $T$ and input head at $p$, the result is the evaluation configuration over the initialization base at $p$, with control in the main dispatch state, table cursor $2|\beta|+2+n+1$, state tape encoding state index $n$, and state cursor $1$.
hypotheses_covered: A bit string $x$ and input-head position $p$ on $x$
replaced:
Suppose the captured table $T$ is the pair encoding of a bit string $\beta$
(the count field) with a string of the form $1^n \cdot 0 \cdot \rho$ (the
initial state $n$ in unary, followed by an arbitrary remainder $\rho$).
Then from the interpreter's entry configuration with physical input head
parked at a position $p$, exactly $|T| + 2|\beta| + 2n + 7$ interpreter steps
reach the evaluation configuration over the initialization base at $p$ whose
control is the main dispatch state, with table cursor $2|\beta| + 2 + n + 1$
(just past the serialized header), the unary state tape encoding the index
$n$, and state cursor $1$.  No transition-table lookup is involved yet.
